newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on outlooks for rain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on outlooks for rain.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on forecasts for rain by this weekend in key corn growing areas of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"If it gets wetter we may go down further and if it gets drier we may go up," said Smith Barney analyst Dale Gustafson. "If we don't know by Friday, Monday could be an interesting day again."

Monday this week corn rallied the 12-cent limit in some months on a drier-than-expected weekend in the Midwest and forecasts for hotter and drier weather this week in key U.S. corn growing states, especially in central Illinois.

Meteorologists early Wednesday said two rain systems were forecast to move across the U.S. Midwest between now and early next week, with the second system offering the best chance of rain for dry areas in central Illinois.
The U.S. corn crop is in the early days of pollination, which is the key reproductive stage of development.
Extreme heat and dry weather during pollination interferes with the formation of corn kernels and cuts into corn yields.
Corn closed three to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with July down 4-1/4 at $2.66-1/2 a bushel. December closed 5-3/4 cents lower at $2.50-3/4 a bushel.

As of Sunday, seven percent of the crop was silking (pollinating), USDA reported. Talk circulated that roughly 20 percent of the crop will have pollinated by this weekend, leaving about 80 percent to go through that key stage.

LIT America sold three million bushels of December and Smith Barney sold two million December, traders said. Refco Inc traded six million December, Cargill Inc bought four million December and bought five million September and Cargill Investor Services bought ten million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, Cargill Inc did 2.5 million bushels of December/September at even money and did two million September/July at 14 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, below Tuesday's actual volume of 126,035.

In corn options, Iowa Grain bought 500 December $2.50 puts at 13 to 13-1/4 cents, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 1,000 December $3.00 calls at four cents and USA Trading bought 500 September $3.00 calls at two cents and sold 1,000 September $3.30 calls at 5/8 cent, traders said.
Options volume was pegged at 33,000 contracts, against Tuesday's 41,316.
